title: Gender Bias of LLM in Economics: An Existentialism Perspective
benchmark_measurement: The paper discusses religion's role in shaping societal gender stereotypes but does not empirically measure religious bias or any aspect of religion with its benchmarks. The discussion is philosophical, framing religion as one of several societal institutions (law, education, family) that collectively construct and sustain gender norms.
findings: The paper posits that institutions like religion contribute to an 'intersubjective network' that constructs and sustains gender norms. It argues that traditional religious teachings can prescribe specific gender roles, thus reinforcing biases. However, it also notes that religious institutions are capable of evolution, with 'progressive theological perspectives' and new interpretations of religious texts increasingly challenging traditional biases and supporting gender equality.
